subject.title: Npm-valid package scopes with dots/underscores cannot map to ClawHub publishers

question: Should ClawHub treat npm-compatible dotted and underscored scopes as valid publisher identities now that the behavior is implemented and released?
rationale: The code path is already implemented, but the issue is collaborator-authored and asks for an intentional ownership/security policy choice rather than only a mechanical fix.

options.title: Accept npm-compatible handles
options.body: Keep the current validation that allows dots and underscores in publisher handles and close this issue as the accepted policy.

options.title: Design scope aliases
options.body: Keep this issue open until a first-class scope-to-publisher alias model is specified and implemented.

options.title: Require package renames
options.body: Reject dotted and underscored publisher handles and document a migration path for affected packages to rename their npm scopes.

recommendation.title: Accept npm-compatible handles
recommendation.body: Keep the current validation that allows dots and underscores in publisher handles and close this issue as the accepted policy.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the policy issue and the merged implementation currently defining the behavior.
